name: Fast CRC32 (Sarwate / Slicing-by-8 / Slicing-by-16)
workload: CRC32 checksum of a 1 GiB in-memory buffer, single-threaded, x86-64 desktop
claimed_speedup: Slicing-by-8: 1800/1400 MByte/s; Slicing-by-16: 3000-3200 MByte/s, vs 375 MByte/s for the standard Sarwate byte-table implementation (~4.3x-8.5x) and vs 35 MByte/s for the naive bitwise version (~50-90x, implausible/capped)
compiler_and_flags: GCC 4.7 and Visual C++ 2010 compared for Slicing-by-4/8/16; GCC 4.7 produces faster code
hardware: Intel Core i7 860 (2.8 GHz, Turbo Boost 3.2 GHz)
tradeoffs: Slicing-by-N trades table memory (up to 16KB) for speed; purely software/table-based, no PCLMULQDQ/SSE4.2 hardware CRC path, so slower than hardware-accelerated CRC32C libraries; single-header C++ library, usable from C via a thin wrapper
caveats: Benchmark hardware/compilers are from the 2011-2015 era (Core i7 860, GCC 4.7, VC++2010); no commits since 2021; the vs-'Original bitwise' comparison (~90x) is capped at C-level plausibility per the >50x rule, but the vs-Sarwate comparison (the algorithm zlib's own crc32() uses) is the ~4-8x figure reported here and is plausible
found_via: GitHub: gh api graphql search 'topic:crc32 stars:>20', opened https://github.com/stbrumme/crc32 then the linked benchmark page https://create.stephan-brumme.com/crc32/

name: crc-fast (PHP extension)
baseline: PHP native crc32(), hash('crc32'), and hash('crc32c')
workload: CRC-32/ISCSI, CRC-32/ISO-HDLC ('crc32b') and CRC-32/PHP checksums over 1 MiB random payloads
claimed_speedup: ~4x on x86_64 (Intel Sapphire Rapids: 108.1 vs 27.0 GiB/s; AMD Genoa: 53.7 vs 13.6 GiB/s); ~73-233x on aarch64 (AWS Graviton4: 52.3 vs 0.4 GiB/s; Apple M3 Ultra: 99.6 vs 0.4 GiB/s) because PHP has no hardware SIMD CRC32 path on aarch64
hardware: EC2 c7i.metal-48xl (Intel Sapphire Rapids), EC2 c7a.metal-48xl (AMD Genoa), EC2 c8g.metal-48xl (AWS Graviton4), Apple Mac Studio M3 Ultra (32-core)
stars_or_usage: 6 stars; README states production use at Flickr and SmugMug
tradeoffs: Requires building/installing the separate crc-fast-rust shared library plus this C glue extension; adds many CRC-32/CRC-64 variants beyond PHP's three built-ins; not supported on Windows
caveats: First-party README benchmark table names hardware but not compiler/build flags or full methodology beyond '1MiB random payloads', so capped at Tier C; thin PHP binding around the already-catalogued awesomized/crc-fast-rust engine, included here because this specific repo (the PHP extension) is not itself on the known list
